questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A global conglomerate operates 400 AWS accounts structured within AWS Organizations. The central security compliance team mandates that member account administrators and root users must be strictly prevented from creating unencrypted Amazon S3 buckets, provisioning unencrypted EBS volumes, or disabling AWS CloudTrail trails across all AWS Regions. Furthermore, automated CI/CD deployment pipelines residing in a dedicated Shared-Infrastructure OU must maintain full administrative control to manage customer managed keys (CMKs) in AWS KMS. Which architecture enforces these guardrails with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy IAM Permission Boundaries to every IAM role across all 400 member accounts using AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks, adding explicit deny statements for unencrypted storage actions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Permission Boundaries do not restrict the member account root user, do not apply to service-linked roles automatically, and require extensive administrative maintenance across 400 accounts.

options.text: Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) to the Root container of AWS Organizations with explicit Deny statements for unencrypted S3 and EBS actions, and place the Shared-Infrastructure OU outside the Root hierarchy.
options.explanation: Incorrect: In AWS Organizations, all Organizational Units and member accounts must reside under the Root container; an OU cannot be placed outside the Root container hierarchy.

options.text: Attach Service Control Policies (SCPs) with explicit Deny conditions at the intermediate OU levels for unencrypted S3 bucket creation, unencrypted EBS volume provisioning, and CloudTrail modification, while applying a dedicated SCP to the Shared-Infrastructure OU that leaves KMS management permissions unconstrained.
options.explanation: Correct: Service Control Policies (SCPs) applied at OU levels enforce preventive guardrails that apply to all principals (including the root user) within member accounts without affecting sibling OUs or requiring per-account IAM maintenance.

options.text: Deploy AWS Config managed rules across all accounts using AWS CloudFormation StackSets to detect unencrypted S3 buckets and trigger Lambda functions to terminate non-compliant resources.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Config is a detective mechanism that acts after resources are created, failing the mandatory requirement to strictly prevent the creation of non-compliant resources at the API level.

questions.generalExplanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations establish preventive boundaries that restrict all principals (including root) across member accounts. Applying granular SCPs at intermediate OU levels protects accounts without disrupting specific administrative privileges needed in dedicated OUs.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Projetar Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Um conglomerado global opera 400 contas AWS estruturadas no AWS Organizations. A equipe central de conformidade de segurança exige que administradores e o usuário root de contas-membro sejam estritamente impedidos de criar buckets do Amazon S3 não criptografados, provisionar volumes EBS não criptografados ou desativar trilhas do AWS CloudTrail em qualquer Região AWS. Além disso, pipelines de implantação automatizados de CI/CD em uma OU dedicada de Infraestrutura Compartilhada devem manter controle administrativo total para gerenciar chaves KMS gerenciadas pelo cliente (CMKs). Qual arquitetura impõe esses guardrails com a MENOR sobrecarga operacional?

options.text: Implantar IAM Permission Boundaries em todas as roles do IAM em todas as 400 contas-membro usando runbooks do AWS Systems Manager Automation, inserindo negações para ações de armazenamento não criptografado.
options.explanation: Incorreto: As Permission Boundaries do IAM não restringem o usuário root das contas-membro, não se aplicam a service-linked roles automaticamente e exigem manutenção massiva em 400 contas.

options.text: Anexar uma Service Control Policy (SCP) ao contêiner Raiz do AWS Organizations com declarações de Deny explícitas para ações de S3 e EBS sem criptografia, e posicionar a OU de Infraestrutura Compartilhada fora da hierarquia Raiz.
options.explanation: Incorreto: No AWS Organizations, todas as Unidades Organizacionais e contas-membro devem residir obrigatoriamente sob o contêiner Raiz (Root); uma OU não pode ser posicionada fora da hierarquia Raiz.

options.text: Anexar Service Control Policies (SCPs) com condições de Deny explícitas nos níveis intermediários de OU para criação de S3 não criptografado, provisionamento de EBS não criptografado e alteração do CloudTrail, aplicando uma SCP dedicada à OU de Infraestrutura Compartilhada que mantém permissões de KMS irrestritas.
options.explanation: Correto: As SCPs aplicadas nos níveis de OU impõem guardrails preventivos que se aplicam a todos os principais (inclusive o usuário root) dentro das contas-membro, sem impactar OUs irmãs e sem exigir manutenção individual de IAM em cada conta.

options.text: Implantar regras gerenciadas do AWS Config em todas as contas usando AWS CloudFormation StackSets para detectar buckets S3 não criptografados e acionar funções Lambda para excluir recursos não conformes.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O AWS Config é uma ferramenta detectiva que atua após o recurso ser criado, violando a exigência mandatória de impedir preventivamente a criação de recursos fora de conformidade na camada de API.

pt.generalExplanation: As Service Control Policies (SCPs) no AWS Organizations estabelecem limites preventivos que restringem todos os principais (incluindo root) nas contas-membro. A aplicação de SCPs granulares nos níveis intermediários de OU protege as contas sem prejudicar privilégios administrativos necessários em OUs dedicadas.

es.domainName: Dominio 1: Diseñar Soluciones para la Complejidad Organizacional
es.statement: Un conglomerado global opera 400 cuentas de AWS en AWS Organizations. El equipo de seguridad exige que administradores y usuarios root tengan estrictamente prohibido crear buckets S3 sin cifrar, volúmenes EBS sin cifrar o desactivar CloudTrail. Además, los canales de CI/CD en la OU de Infraestructura Compartida deben administrar claves KMS sin restricciones. ¿Qué arquitectura impone estas barreras con la MENOR sobrecarga operativa?

options.text: Desplegar Límites de Permisos de IAM en todos los roles en las 400 cuentas miembro mediante runbooks de Systems Manager Automation con denegaciones de almacenamiento sin cifrar.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Los límites de permisos de IAM no restringen al usuario root de las cuentas miembro y requieren mantenimiento continuo en 400 cuentas frente a políticas centralizadas.

options.text: Adjuntar una Service Control Policy (SCP) al contenedor Raíz de AWS Organizations con Deny explícito para S3 y EBS sin cifrar y ubicar la OU de Infraestructura Compartida fuera de la Raíz.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: En AWS Organizations, todas las OUs y cuentas miembro deben residir bajo el contenedor Raíz; una OU no puede ubicarse fuera de la jerarquía Raíz.

options.text: Adjuntar Service Control Policies (SCPs) con condiciones de Deny explícitas en los niveles intermedios de OU para S3 y EBS sin cifrar y modificación de CloudTrail, aplicando una SCP dedicada a la OU de Infraestructura Compartida sin restricciones de KMS.
options.explanation: Correcto: Las SCPs aplicadas en niveles de OU imponen barreras preventivas que se aplican a todos los principales (incluido el usuario root) dentro de las cuentas miembro sin afectar a las OUs hermanas.

options.text: Desplegar reglas administradas de AWS Config mediante CloudFormation StackSets para detectar buckets S3 sin cifrar y activar funciones Lambda para eliminar recursos no conformes.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: AWS Config es un mecanismo detectivesco que actúa después de que se crean los recursos, fallando el requisito obligatorio de prevenir estrictamente a nivel de API.

es.generalExplanation: Las Service Control Policies (SCPs) en AWS Organizations establecen barreras preventivas que restringen a todos los principales (incluido el root) en las cuentas miembro sin afectar privilegios específicos en OUs dedicadas.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: An enterprise connects 100 production and non-production VPCs across multiple AWS accounts to an AWS Transit Gateway. The security architecture mandates complete network segmentation: non-production VPCs must never communicate with production VPCs, while all outbound internet traffic from both environments must be inspected by stateful firewalls in a centralized Egress VPC. The solution must support independent route table isolation and preserve packet symmetry across multiple Availability Zones without using Source NAT. Which Transit Gateway routing architecture satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create separate Transit Gateway Route Tables for Production, Non-Production, and Egress. Associate production VPCs with the Production route table, non-production VPCs with the Non-Production route table, and route default 0.0.0.0/0 traffic to the Egress VPC attachment configured with Transit Gateway Appliance Mode.
options.explanation: Correct: Transit Gateway route domains isolate routing environments completely, preventing non-prod from reaching prod, while directing default egress traffic through the Appliance Mode-enabled inspection VPC.

options.text: Configure a single default Transit Gateway route table and attach an IAM policy to all EC2 instances in non-production VPCs that denies outbound network packets to production IP ranges.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM policies control AWS API calls; they cannot filter or inspect Layer 3/4 network IP packets flowing between VPCs.

options.text: Establish bidirectional VPC Peering between all 100 VPCs and deploy AWS Network Firewall endpoints directly in each spoke VPC subnet. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Full-mesh VPC Peering across 100 accounts creates severe routing management overhead (4,950 peering links) and violates the centralized egress inspection requirement.

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer in each non-production VPC with path-based routing rules that reject requests containing production headers. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: ALBs operate at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and cannot provide Layer 3 network routing segmentation between multi-account enterprise VPCs.

questions.generalExplanation: Creating dedicated Transit Gateway Route Tables for Production, Non-Production, and Egress domains, associating each VPC with its designated route table, and enabling Transit Gateway Appliance Mode on the Egress VPC attachment provides secure domain segmentation with symmetric stateful inspection.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Projetar Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma empresa conecta 100 VPCs de produção e não-produção em múltiplas contas AWS a um AWS Transit Gateway. A arquitetura de segurança exige segmentação completa de rede: VPCs de não-produção nunca devem se comunicar com VPCs de produção, enquanto todo o tráfego de saída para a internet de ambos os ambientes deve ser inspecionado por firewalls com estado em uma VPC de Egresso centralizada. A solução deve suportar isolamento independente de tabelas de rotas e preservar a simetria de pacotes entre múltiplas Zonas de Disponibilidade sem usar Source NAT. Qual arquitetura de roteamento do Transit Gateway atende a esses requisitos?

options.text: Criar tabelas de rotas separadas do Transit Gateway para Produção, Não-Produção e Egresso. Associar VPCs de produção à tabela de Produção, VPCs de não-produção à tabela de Não-Produção e rotear o tráfego padrão 0.0.0.0/0 para o anexo da VPC de Egresso configurado com Transit Gateway Appliance Mode.
options.explanation: Correto: Os domínios de rota do Transit Gateway isolam ambientes de roteamento completamente, impedindo que não-produção alcance produção, enquanto direcionam o tráfego padrão de egresso através da VPC de inspeção com Appliance Mode ativado.

options.text: Configurar uma única tabela de rotas padrão do Transit Gateway e anexar uma política IAM a todas as instâncias EC2 nas VPCs de não-produção negando pacotes de rede para faixas IP de produção.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Políticas do IAM controlam chamadas de API da AWS; elas não conseguem filtrar ou inspecionar pacotes de rede IP de Camada 3/4 trafegando entre VPCs.

options.text: Estabelecer VPC Peering bidirecional entre todas as 100 VPCs e implantar endpoints do AWS Network Firewall diretamente na sub-rede de cada VPC spoke.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Uma malha completa de VPC Peering em 100 contas gera altíssima sobrecarga de gestão de rotas (4.950 links de peering) e viola a exigência de inspeção de egresso centralizada.

options.text: Implantar um Application Load Balancer em cada VPC de não-produção com regras de roteamento baseadas em caminho que rejeitam requisições contendo cabeçalhos de produção.
options.explanation: Incorreto: ALBs operam na Camada 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) e não conseguem fornecer segmentação de roteamento de rede de Camada 3 entre VPCs corporativas.

pt.generalExplanation: A criação de tabelas de rotas dedicadas do Transit Gateway para os domínios de Produção, Não-Produção e Egresso, associando cada VPC à sua tabela de rotas designada e habilitando o Appliance Mode no anexo de VPC de Egresso fornece segmentação segura de domínios com inspeção simétrica com estado.

es.domainName: Dominio 1: Diseñar Soluciones para la Complejidad Organizacional
es.statement: Una empresa conecta 100 VPCs de producción y no producción a un AWS Transit Gateway. Se exige segmentación completa: no producción nunca debe comunicarse con producción y todo el tráfico saliente a internet debe inspeccionarse en una VPC de Egreso central. La solución debe aislar tablas de rutas y mantener simetría de paquetes en múltiples Zonas de Disponibilidad sin Source NAT. ¿Qué arquitectura de enrutamiento cumple estos requisitos?

options.text: Crear tablas de rutas independientes en Transit Gateway para Producción, No Producción y Egreso. Asociar VPCs según su entorno y enrutar el tráfico 0.0.0.0/0 hacia el adjunto de la VPC de Egreso con Appliance Mode habilitado.
options.explanation: Correcto: Las tablas de rutas de Transit Gateway aíslan completamente los entornos de red y dirigen el tráfico saliente por defecto hacia la VPC de inspección con Appliance Mode habilitado.

options.text: Configurar una única tabla de rutas en Transit Gateway y adjuntar políticas de IAM a las instancias EC2 para bloquear paquetes hacia producción.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Las políticas de IAM controlan llamadas a la API de AWS y no pueden filtrar tráfico de red de Capa 3/4 entre VPCs.

options.text: Establecer VPC Peering entre las 100 VPCs y desplegar endpoints de AWS Network Firewall en cada subred spoke. Este paso de configuración arquitectónica garantiza el pleno cumplimiento de las mejores prácticas empresariales de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Una malla completa de VPC Peering entre 100 cuentas genera una complejidad inmanejable y viola el requisito de inspección centralizada.

options.text: Desplegar un Application Load Balancer en cada VPC de no producción con reglas de enrutamiento basadas en rutas. Este paso de configuración arquitectónica garantiza el pleno cumplimiento de las mejores prácticas empresariales de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Los balanceadores de aplicación operan en Capa 7 y no proporcionan segmentación de red de Capa 3 entre VPCs.

es.generalExplanation: Crear tablas de rutas dedicadas en Transit Gateway para Producción, No Producción y Egreso, asociando cada VPC a su tabla correspondiente y habilitando Appliance Mode en el adjunto de la VPC de Egreso proporciona segmentación segura con inspección simétrica con estado.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A global enterprise connects its on-premises corporate data centers in New York and London to 150 AWS VPCs in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 using two 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connections. The network engineering team requires active/active routing where traffic originating in the New York data center prefers the local us-east-1 Region, while traffic originating in London prefers the local eu-west-1 Region. Furthermore, cross-region failover must happen automatically across the AWS global backbone if a local Direct Connect connection fails. Which BGP routing architecture should the network architect deploy?

options.text: Configure 150 Private Virtual Interfaces (Private VIFs) directly from each Direct Connect connection to every individual VPC Virtual Private Gateway. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Direct Connect connections support a maximum of 50 Private VIFs and direct VIFs do not support multi-region Transit Gateway routing or automated cross-region backbone failover.

options.text: Deploy IPsec VPN tunnels over the public internet between on-premises routers and an Application Load Balancer in each region. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard IPsec VPN tunnels over the public internet have bandwidth limits (1.25 Gbps), variable latency, and cannot terminate on Application Load Balancers.

options.text: Establish full-mesh VPC Peering between all 150 VPCs across both regions and configure static IP host routes on local data center core switches.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Inter-region VPC Peering across 150 VPCs creates exponential routing complexity and static routes do not support dynamic active/active failover.

options.text: Deploy a centralized Direct Connect Gateway associated with regional AWS Transit Gateways in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 using Transit Virtual Interfaces (Transit VIFs). Use BGP communities (such as 7224:7300 for local preference) on advertised routes from each data center to prefer local regional ingress, enabling automatic backbone failover.
options.explanation: Correct: Direct Connect Gateway with Transit VIFs connects data centers to regional Transit Gateways. BGP communities allow granular local preference path control across global AWS regions with seamless failover.

questions.generalExplanation: Using a Direct Connect Gateway associated with regional Transit Gateways and advertising BGP prefixes tagged with AWS BGP Local Preference communities (such as 7224:7300 for local region preference) enables deterministic path selection and automatic backbone failover.

pt.statement: Uma empresa global conecta seus data centers corporativos on-premises em Nova York e Londres a 150 VPCs na AWS em us-east-1 e eu-west-1 usando duas conexões dedicadas de 10 Gbps do AWS Direct Connect. Além disso, o failover cross-region deve ocorrer automaticamente através do backbone global da AWS se uma conexão local do Direct Connect falhar. Qual arquitetura de roteamento BGP o arquiteto de rede deve implantar?

options.text: Configurar 150 Private Virtual Interfaces (Private VIFs) diretamente de cada conexão do Direct Connect para cada Virtual Private Gateway de VPC individual.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Conexões do Direct Connect suportam um máximo de 50 Private VIFs e VIFs diretas não suportam roteamento de Transit Gateway multirregião nem failover automático pelo backbone.

options.text: Implantar túneis VPN IPsec pela internet pública entre roteadores on-premises e um Application Load Balancer em cada região. Esta etapa de configuração arquitetural garante total conformidade com as melhores práticas corporativas do AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Túneis VPN IPsec pela internet pública possuem limites de largura de banda (1,25 Gbps), latência instável e não podem terminar em Application Load Balancers.

options.text: Estabelecer VPC Peering em malha completa entre todas as 150 VPCs em ambas as regiões e configurar rotas estáticas de host nos switches centrais do data center local.
options.explanation: Incorreto: VPC Peering inter-região em 150 VPCs cria complexidade exponencial de roteamento e rotas estáticas não suportam failover dinâmico ativo/ativo.

options.text: Implantar um Direct Connect Gateway centralizado associado a AWS Transit Gateways regionais em us-east-1 e eu-west-1 usando Transit Virtual Interfaces (Transit VIFs). options.explanation: Correto: O Direct Connect Gateway com Transit VIFs conecta data centers a Transit Gateways regionais. O uso de comunidades BGP permite controle granular de preferência de caminho local com failover transparente entre regiões.

pt.generalExplanation: O uso de um Direct Connect Gateway associado a Transit Gateways regionais e o anúncio de prefixos BGP com tags de comunidades BGP da AWS (como 7224:7300 para preferência de região local) viabiliza seleção determinística de caminho e failover automático pelo backbone da AWS.

Which combination of mechanisms satisfies these security requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda function that scans IAM roles every 10 minutes and deletes roles containing unauthorized permissions. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Reactive Lambda polling allows unauthorized roles to exist and execute actions between scan intervals, failing the preventive requirement.

options.text: Require an IAM Permissions Boundary policy attached to all developer IAM roles, enforcing that developers cannot create or modify roles without attaching the mandatory boundary policy.
options.explanation: Correct: IAM Permission Boundaries set the maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant to an IAM role, preventing developers from escalating privileges.

options.text: Attach an AWS WAF Web ACL to all VPC endpoints to filter out IAM API requests containing admin actions. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS WAF inspects HTTP/HTTPS traffic to application endpoints (ALB/CloudFront/API Gateway); it does not inspect or intercept AWS IAM control plane API calls.

options.text: Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) to the Sandbox OU with explicit Deny conditions for ec2:RunInstances on unauthorized instance types (such as p4d.*) and Deny on cloudtrail:DeleteTrail and cloudtrail:StopLogging.

Qual combinação de mecanismos atende a esses requisitos de segurança? (Escolha duas.)

options.explanation: Incorreto: A varredura reativa por Lambda permite que roles não autorizadas existam e executem ações entre os intervalos de varredura, falhando na exigência preventiva.

options.text: Exigir uma política de IAM Permissions Boundary anexada a todas as roles de desenvolvedores, garantindo que não possam criar ou modificar roles sem anexar a política de boundary obrigatória.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A global enterprise is integrating its corporate Okta identity provider with AWS Organizations managing 300 accounts. The identity architecture must provide Single Sign-On (SSO) for 10,000 corporate users across all AWS accounts, enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) at the IdP layer, automatically synchronize user provisioning and deprovisioning without manual credential maintenance in AWS, and assign permissions centrally based on corporate job roles. Which combination of steps should the enterprise implement? (Choose three.)

options.text: Enable AWS IAM Identity Center in the AWS Organizations management account and select External identity provider as the identity source. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Correct: Enabling IAM Identity Center in the management account allows centralizing multi-account workforce access and federating with external IdPs.

options.text: Create individual IAM users with virtual MFA tokens in every one of the 300 member accounts and write custom scripts to sync passwords.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Managing 10,000 users across 300 accounts (3 million credentials) is a massive administrative anti-pattern that violates enterprise SSO standards.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Cognito User Pool in each member account and configure AWS Lambda triggers to issue temporary STS credentials. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Cognito User Pools is designed for customer-facing consumer apps, not workforce enterprise SSO across AWS Organizations.

options.text: Configure SAML 2.0 federation by exchanging metadata between Okta and AWS IAM Identity Center to enable Single Sign-On and enforce corporate MFA.
options.explanation: Correct: SAML 2.0 metadata exchange establishes mutual trust between Okta and AWS IAM Identity Center, enabling secure SSO and delegating MFA to Okta.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Directory Service for Microsoft AD in each member account and establish two-way transitive forest trusts. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deploying Managed AD in 300 accounts generates massive licensing costs and ongoing infrastructure management overhead.

options.text: Enable System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) automatic provisioning in Okta using the SCIM endpoint and access token from IAM Identity Center, and assign permission sets to synchronized Okta groups across target AWS accounts.
options.explanation: Correct: SCIM automatically syncs user creations, updates, and deactivations from Okta to AWS, while permission sets mapped to groups enforce role-based access across accounts.

questions.generalExplanation: Integrating AWS IAM Identity Center with Okta requires: (1) Enabling IAM Identity Center in the AWS Organizations management account, (2) Configuring SAML 2.0 federation between Okta and IAM Identity Center for SSO and MFA, and (3) Enabling SCIM automatic provisioning in Okta to sync users and groups and assigning permission sets to groups across AWS accounts.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: An enterprise with 200 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations has on-premises data centers connected via AWS Direct Connect. The enterprise maintains internal on-premises DNS zones (corp.internal) and internal AWS Route 53 private hosted zones. Amazon EC2 instances in all 200 accounts must be able to resolve corp.internal domain names, while on-premises corporate users must resolve AWS private hosted zones. The network architecture requires centralizing hybrid DNS forwarding in a single Central Network Account and sharing DNS forwarding rules across all 200 accounts with zero per-VPC server provisioning. Which solution should the architect implement?

options.text: Deploy custom BIND DNS forwarder EC2 instances in each of the 200 accounts and configure cron jobs to synchronize zone files over VPC Peering.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Maintaining 200 pairs of custom BIND servers creates massive operational patching and high availability overhead compared to managed Route 53 Resolver.

options.text: Deploy Route 53 Resolver Outbound Endpoints and Inbound Endpoints in the Central Network Account. Create a Route 53 Resolver forwarding rule for corp.internal pointing to the on-premises DNS server IPs, and share the rule with the entire organization using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
options.explanation: Correct: Route 53 Resolver Outbound Endpoints forward queries to on-premises DNS, and sharing the rule via AWS RAM allows all 200 accounts to resolve on-premises domains seamlessly without local DNS servers.

options.text: Modify DHCP Option Sets in all 200 accounts to set on-premises DNS IP addresses as the primary domain name servers. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Setting DHCP options to on-premises DNS breaks resolution for Amazon VPC-provided DNS endpoints and local AWS service metadata.

options.text: Make all private hosted zones public in Route 53 and create public DNS records for all internal EC2 instances. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Making internal hosted zones public exposes private infrastructure names and IP addresses to the public internet, violating security compliance.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying Route 53 Resolver Outbound and Inbound Endpoints in the Central Network Account and sharing Route 53 Resolver forwarding rules across the organization using AWS RAM enables seamless hybrid DNS resolution without per-VPC server management.

A empresa mantém zonas DNS internas on-premises (corp.internal) e zonas hospedadas privadas do Route 53 na AWS. Instâncias Amazon EC2 em todas as 200 contas devem ser capazes de resolver nomes de domínio corp.internal, enquanto usuários corporativos on-premises devem resolver zonas hospedadas privadas da AWS. A arquitetura de rede exige centralizar o encaminhamento de DNS híbrido em uma única Conta Central de Rede e compartilhar regras de encaminhamento de DNS em todas as 200 contas sem provisionar servidores em cada VPC. Qual solução o arquiteto deve implementar?

options.text: Implantar instâncias EC2 com encaminhadores DNS BIND customizados em cada uma das 200 contas e configurar tarefas cron para sincronizar arquivos de zona sobre VPC Peering.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Manter 200 pares de servidores BIND customizados cria altíssima sobrecarga operacional de aplicação de patches e alta disponibilidade em comparação com o Route 53 Resolver gerenciado.

options.text: Implantar Route 53 Resolver Outbound Endpoints e Inbound Endpoints na Conta Central de Rede. Criar uma regra de encaminhamento do Route 53 Resolver para corp.internal apontando para os IPs de servidores DNS on-premises e compartilhar a regra com toda a organização usando o AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
options.explanation: Correto: Os Outbound Endpoints do Route 53 Resolver encaminham consultas para o DNS on-premises, e o compartilhamento da regra via AWS RAM permite que todas as 200 contas resolvam domínios on-premises sem necessidade de servidores DNS locais.

options.text: Modificar os DHCP Option Sets em todas as 200 contas para definir os endereços IP do DNS on-premises como servidores de nomes de domínio primários.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Alterar DHCP options para DNS on-premises quebra a resolução de endpoints fornecidos pela Amazon VPC e metadados de serviços locais da AWS.

options.text: Tornar todas as zonas hospedadas privadas públicas no Route 53 e criar registros DNS públicos para todas as instâncias EC2 internas. Esta etapa de configuração arquitetural garante total conformidade com as melhores práticas corporativas do AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Tornar públicas as zonas privadas expõe nomes de infraestrutura interna e endereços IP à internet pública, violando conformidade de segurança.

pt.generalExplanation: A implantação de Route 53 Resolver Outbound e Inbound Endpoints na Conta Central de Rede e o compartilhamento de regras de encaminhamento do Route 53 Resolver em toda a organização via AWS RAM permite resolução híbrida de DNS transparente sem gestão de servidores por VPC.

es.domainName: Dominio 1: Diseñar Soluciones para la Complejidad Organizacional
es.statement: Una empresa con 200 cuentas en AWS Organizations tiene centros de datos locales conectados por Direct Connect. Se mantienen zonas DNS internas (corp.internal) y zonas privadas de Route 53. Las instancias EC2 en las 200 cuentas deben resolver corp.internal y los usuarios locales deben resolver zonas privadas de AWS. Se exige centralizar el reenvío de DNS híbrido en una Cuenta Central de Red y compartir reglas sin servidores dedicados por VPC. ¿Qué solución debe implementar el arquitecto?

options.text: Desplegar instancias EC2 con servidores BIND en cada una de las 200 cuentas y sincronizar zonas mediante cron por VPC Peering. Este paso de configuración arquitectónica garantiza el pleno cumplimiento de las mejores prácticas empresariales de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Administrar servidores BIND en 200 cuentas genera una carga operativa inmensa de parches y alta disponibilidad.

options.text: Desplegar Route 53 Resolver Outbound e Inbound Endpoints en la Cuenta Central de Red. Crear una regla de reenvío para corp.internal hacia las IPs locales y compartirla con toda la organización mediante AWS RAM.
options.explanation: Correcto: Route 53 Resolver Outbound Endpoints reenvía consultas a DNS locales y compartir la regla mediante AWS RAM permite a las 200 cuentas resolver dominios locales sin servidores dedicados.

options.text: Modificar DHCP Option Sets en las 200 cuentas para establecer las IPs de DNS locales como servidores primarios. Este paso de configuración arquitectónica garantiza el pleno cumplimiento de las mejores prácticas empresariales de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Apuntar DHCP Option Sets directamente a DNS locales interrumpe la resolución de DNS provisto por VPC y metadatos de instancias.

options.text: Hacer públicas todas las zonas privadas de Route 53 publicando registros DNS de todas las instancias internas. Este paso de configuración arquitectónica garantiza el pleno cumplimiento de las mejores prácticas empresariales de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Publicar zonas privadas en DNS público expone información interna confidencial y vulnera la seguridad corporativa.

es.generalExplanation: Desplegar Route 53 Resolver Inbound y Outbound Endpoints en la Cuenta Central de Red y compartir reglas de reenvío en toda la organización mediante AWS RAM permite resolución híbrida sin servidores por VPC.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A high-frequency trading firm deploys an ultra-low latency order matching engine on AWS. The application requires sub-millisecond network communication between distributed matching engine nodes, 100 Gbps network throughput with low inter-instance jitter, and in-memory transactional caching with Multi-AZ durability and microsecond response times. Which architecture delivers the HIGHEST performance and lowest latency?

options.text: Deploy instances in a Spread Placement Group across three AWS Regions connected via AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnels. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Spread placement groups across multiple regions introduce inter-region network latencies of 50-100ms over VPN, failing the sub-millisecond requirement.

options.text: Deploy instances in a Partition Placement Group with 7 partitions per Availability Zone, and use Amazon RDS PostgreSQL Single-AZ with standard gp2 storage.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Partition placement groups do not guarantee close physical proximity for low-latency node communication, and standard gp2 storage introduces disk I/O latency bottlenecks.

options.text: Launch compute-optimized Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) enabled inside a Cluster Placement Group within a single Availability Zone. Use Amazon MemoryDB for Redis configured with Multi-AZ transactional logging as the primary state store.
options.explanation: Correct: Cluster Placement Groups place instances physically close together on high-speed network fabric for 100 Gbps low-jitter interconnects, while MemoryDB delivers microsecond read/write performance with Multi-AZ ACID durability.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) cluster on AWS Fargate with tasks distributed across multiple AWS Regions behind Amazon CloudFront. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Fargate does not support Cluster Placement Groups or Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), and CloudFront edge routing is designed for web caching, not high-frequency node communication.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying compute-optimized Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) inside a Cluster Placement Group within a single Availability Zone, backed by Amazon MemoryDB for Redis with Multi-AZ transactional logging, delivers ultra-low network latency and microsecond in-memory state persistence.

pt.statement: Uma empresa de trading de alta frequência implanta um mecanismo de correspondência de ordens de ultra-baixa latência na AWS. options.text: Implantar instâncias em um grupo de posicionamento de dispersão (Spread) em três Regiões AWS conectadas via túneis AWS Site-to-Site VPN. Esta etapa de configuração arquitetural garante total conformidade com as melhores práticas corporativas do AWS Well-Architected Framework.

options.text: Implantar instâncias em um grupo de posicionamento de partição com 7 partições por Zona de Disponibilidade e usar o Amazon RDS PostgreSQL Single-AZ com armazenamento gp2 padrão.

options.text: Iniciar instâncias Amazon EC2 otimizadas para computação com Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) habilitado dentro de um Cluster Placement Group em uma única Zona de Disponibilidade. Usar o Amazon MemoryDB for Redis configurado com log transacional Multi-AZ como armazenamento primário de estado.
options.explanation: Correto: Cluster Placement Groups posicionam instâncias fisicamente próximas na mesma infraestrutura de rede de alta velocidade para interconexão de 100 Gbps com baixo jitter, enquanto o MemoryDB fornece leitura/gravação em microssegundos com durabilidade ACID Multi-AZ.

pt.generalExplanation: A implantação de instâncias Amazon EC2 otimizadas para computação com Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) dentro de um Cluster Placement Group em uma única Zona de Disponibilidade, sustentadas pelo Amazon MemoryDB for Redis com log transacional Multi-AZ, oferece latência de rede ultra-baixa e persistência de estado em memória em microssegundos.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A multinational travel agency processes booking reservations across hundreds of microservices. When a customer confirms a flight, hotel, and rental car booking, the booking orchestrator must execute a distributed transaction (Saga pattern) coordinating inventory reservation, payment processing, and confirmation notification. If payment processing fails, compensating transactions must automatically rollback previously reserved flight and hotel slots. The orchestration must handle up to 50,000 bookings per hour, track execution history, and minimize custom error-handling code. Which architecture satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Deploy an AWS Step Functions Standard Workflow orchestrating AWS Lambda functions for each booking step. Configure built-in Retry and Catch blocks to trigger compensating Lambda rollback functions upon failure, and persist transaction state in Amazon DynamoDB.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Step Functions Standard Workflows natively orchestrates distributed microservice transactions (Saga pattern), providing deterministic state transitions, automated retries, compensating rollback workflows, and complete execution auditability.

options.text: Send messages to an Amazon SQS Standard queue and invoke a single monolithic Lambda function that executes all steps sequentially inside a single Python try-catch block.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Monolithic Lambda functions executing multiple external API calls risk timing out, lack visual execution history, and fail to scale reliably under high concurrency.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster and write custom Java consumer group daemons to manage rollback states across EC2 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed Kafka consumer state machines require substantial operational maintenance and custom failure-handling logic compared to native Step Functions state machines.

options.text: Configure Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) to broadcast booking requests to 20 independent Lambda functions simultaneously without orchestration. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SNS fan-out cannot enforce sequential dependencies or coordinate compensating rollback transactions across independent downstream services.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Step Functions Standard Workflows paired with Amazon EventBridge and Amazon DynamoDB implements the Saga pattern natively with built-in retry policies, Catch error handlers, and visual execution history.

Quando um cliente confirma uma reserva de voo, hotel e aluguel de carro, o orquestrador de reservas deve executar uma transação distribuída (padrão Saga) coordenando a reserva de inventário, processamento de pagamento e notificação de confirmação. Se o processamento do pagamento falhar, transações de compensação devem reverter automaticamente os slots de voo e hotel reservados anteriormente. A orquestração deve suportar até 50.000 reservas por hora, rastrear o histórico de execução e minimizar o código customizado de tratamento de erros. Qual arquitetura atende a esses requisitos?

options.text: Implantar um AWS Step Functions Standard Workflow orquestrando funções AWS Lambda para cada etapa de reserva. Configurar blocos integrados de Retry e Catch para acionar funções Lambda de compensação e rollback em caso de falha e persistir o estado da transação no Amazon DynamoDB.
options.explanation: Correto: O AWS Step Functions Standard Workflows orquestra nativamente transações distribuídas de microsserviços (padrão Saga), fornecendo transições determinísticas de estado, repetições automáticas, fluxos de reversão e auditoria visual completa.

options.text: Enviar mensagens para uma fila padrão do Amazon SQS e invocar uma única função Lambda monolítica que executa todas as etapas sequencialmente dentro de um único bloco try-catch em Python.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Funções Lambda monolíticas executando múltiplas chamadas de API externas correm risco de timeout, não possuem histórico visual de execução e falham ao escalar sob alta concorrência.

options.text: Implantar um cluster do Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) e escrever daemons Java customizados de consumer group para gerenciar estados de rollback em instâncias EC2.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Máquinas de estado autogerenciadas em Kafka exigem considerável manutenção operacional e lógica customizada de tratamento de falhas em comparação com o Step Functions.

options.text: Configurar o Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) para transmitir solicitações de reserva para 20 funções Lambda independentes simultaneamente sem orquestração. Esta etapa de configuração arquitetural garante total conformidade com as melhores práticas corporativas do AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O fan-out do SNS não consegue impor dependências sequenciais nem coordenar transações de compensação e rollback entre serviços independentes.

pt.generalExplanation: O AWS Step Functions Standard Workflows combinado com o Amazon EventBridge e o Amazon DynamoDB implementa o padrão Saga nativamente com políticas integradas de repetição, manipuladores de erro Catch e histórico visual de execução.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: An automotive manufacturer collects real-time sensor telematics from 2 million connected vehicles worldwide. Vehicles transmit telemetry payloads every 5 seconds over MQTT. The architecture must ingest up to 400,000 messages per second, enforce secure mutual TLS (mTLS) device authentication, route telemetry streams in real time with sub-second latency for fleet anomaly detection, and continuously archive all raw payloads into an Amazon S3 data lake bucket partitioned by date and vehicle model. Which serverless architecture fulfills these requirements with the HIGHEST scalability?

options.text: Deploy an Auto Scaling group of 200 Amazon EC2 instances running open-source Mosquitto MQTT brokers in public subnets behind an Application Load Balancer.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed MQTT brokers require extensive operational patching, connection balancing, and lack automated serverless scaling to 400,000 messages/sec.

options.text: Configure Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with regional custom domains to receive telemetry via HTTP POST requests, writing directly to an Amazon RDS MySQL database.
options.explanation: Incorrect: API Gateway HTTP APIs do not support persistent MQTT TLS connections and relational RDS databases cannot sustain 400,000 continuous write transactions per second.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon SQS Standard queue to receive MQTT packets and configure a single AWS Lambda function to parse all vehicle payloads.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SQS Standard does not terminate MQTT TLS connections from IoT devices natively and a single Lambda cannot process 400,000 msgs/sec sequentially.

options.text: Connect vehicles directly to AWS IoT Core using X.509 client certificates for mutual TLS authentication. Configure an AWS IoT Topic Rule that routes telemetry payloads to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in On-Demand mode for real-time anomaly detection, and a second IoT Rule that routes payloads to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to convert records into Parquet and partition storage in Amazon S3.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS IoT Core terminates hundreds of thousands of concurrent MQTT mTLS connections seamlessly. Kinesis Data Streams On-Demand enables real-time stream processing, while Kinesis Data Firehose delivers partitioned data into the S3 data lake.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS IoT Core authenticates vehicle devices via X.509 certificates (mTLS). An AWS IoT Topic Rule routes telemetry streams to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for sub-second real-time anomaly detection, while Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose buffers and writes partitioned Parquet data into the Amazon S3 data lake.

pt.statement: Uma fabricante automotiva coleta telemetria de sensores em tempo real de 2 milhões de veículos conectados em todo o mundo. Os veículos transmitem payloads de telemetria a cada 5 segundos sobre MQTT. A arquitetura deve ingerir até 400.000 mensagens por segundo, aplicar autenticação mTLS segura por certificado X.509, rotear fluxos de telemetria em tempo real com latência sub-segundo para detecção de anomalias na frota e arquivar continuamente todos os dados brutos em um data lake no Amazon S3 particionado por data e modelo de veículo. Qual arquitetura serverless atende a esses requisitos com a MAIOR escalabilidade?

options.text: Implantar um grupo de Auto Scaling de 200 instâncias Amazon EC2 executando brokers MQTT Mosquitto open-source em sub-redes públicas atrás de um Application Load Balancer.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Brokers MQTT autogerenciados exigem ampla manutenção de patches, balanceamento complexo de conexões e não possuem escalabilidade serverless automática para 400.000 mensagens/s.

options.text: Configurar HTTP APIs do Amazon API Gateway com domínios personalizados regionais para receber telemetria via requisições HTTP POST, gravando diretamente em um banco Amazon RDS MySQL.
options.explanation: Incorreto: HTTP APIs do API Gateway não suportam conexões persistentes MQTT TLS e bancos de dados relacionais RDS não sustentam 400.000 gravações contínuas por segundo.

options.text: Implantar uma fila padrão do Amazon SQS para receber pacotes MQTT e configurar uma única função AWS Lambda para processar todos os payloads dos veículos.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O SQS Standard não encerra conexões MQTT TLS de dispositivos IoT nativamente e uma única função Lambda não consegue processar 400.000 mensagens/s sequencialmente.

options.text: Conectar os veículos diretamente ao AWS IoT Core usando certificados de cliente X.509 para autenticação mTLS. Configurar uma regra de tópico do AWS IoT que roteia payloads de telemetria para o Amazon Kinesis Data Streams em modo On-Demand para detecção de anomalias em tempo real e uma segunda regra que roteia payloads para o Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose para converter registros em Parquet e particionar o armazenamento no Amazon S3.
options.explanation: Correto: O AWS IoT Core encerra centenas de milhares de conexões MQTT mTLS concorrentes de forma transparente. O Kinesis Data Streams On-Demand permite processamento em tempo real, enquanto o Kinesis Data Firehose entrega dados particionados no data lake do S3.

pt.generalExplanation: O AWS IoT Core autentica os veículos via certificados X.509 (mTLS). Uma regra de tópico do AWS IoT roteia fluxos para o Amazon Kinesis Data Streams para detecção de anomalias em tempo real sub-segundo, enquanto o Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose armazena em buffer e grava dados em formato Parquet no data lake do Amazon S3.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A global banking portal operates in us-east-1 and requires an active/standby disaster recovery strategy to us-west-2 with an RPO of less than 1 second and an RTO of less than 1 minute. The architecture must support write-forwarding for read replicas, continuous automated validation of recovery environment capacity before routing traffic, and deterministic DNS failover controls without depending on the primary region's availability during an outage. Which architecture provides the HIGHEST resilience?

options.text: Deploy Amazon RDS PostgreSQL cross-region read replicas and configure an AWS Lambda function triggered by CloudWatch alarms to promote the replica. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard RDS cross-region read replica promotion takes several minutes, exceeding the 1-minute RTO, and lacks automated readiness validation.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Aurora Global Database with the primary cluster in us-east-1 and a secondary cluster in us-west-2 with write forwarding enabled. Configure AWS Route 53 Application Recovery Controller (ARC) with Readiness Checks on application compute and database resources, using Routing Controls to execute sub-minute traffic failover safely.
options.explanation: Correct: Aurora Global Database provides sub-second physical replication (<1s RPO) and planned/unplanned failover in under 1 minute (RTO < 1 min). Route 53 ARC validates secondary region readiness and executes reliable traffic shifts.

options.text: Configure AWS Backup to take automated EBS snapshots every 10 minutes and copy them to us-west-2. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: 10-minute snapshot intervals violate the sub-second RPO requirement, and rebuilding databases from snapshots takes hours.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon DynamoDB Global Table in us-east-1 and configure weekly batch export jobs to Amazon Redshift in us-west-2. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Batch export jobs to Redshift do not provide transactional relational database support or sub-minute active/standby failover capabilities.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Aurora Global Database provides storage-level replication with typical sub-second latency and local write forwarding, while AWS Route 53 Application Recovery Controller (ARC) enables deterministic multi-region traffic shift backed by continuous Readiness Checks.

Qual arquitetura oferece a MAIOR resiliência?

options.text: Implantar réplicas de leitura cross-region do Amazon RDS PostgreSQL e configurar uma função AWS Lambda acionada por alarmes do CloudWatch para promover a réplica.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A software vendor hosts an internal analytics service in an Amazon VPC. 250 enterprise clients must access the service from their own VPCs over private AWS network infrastructure without exposing public IP addresses and without requiring CIDR range conflict resolution. Furthermore, all incoming client traffic must be inspected by an AWS WAF Web ACL to block common SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks directly on the private service endpoint. Which architecture fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Establish full-mesh VPC Peering between the vendor VPC and all 250 client VPCs, and deploy open-source iptables firewall scripts on all EC2 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Peering fails if client VPC CIDRs overlap with the vendor VPC and cannot scale across 250 external accounts without routing limits.

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer in each client VPC and configure public internet NAT Gateways in all accounts. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Routing through public NAT Gateways exposes API traffic to the internet, violating the private connectivity requirement.

options.text: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the vendor VPC, associate an AWS WAF Web ACL directly with the NLB, and configure the NLB as an AWS PrivateLink Endpoint Service. Instruct clients to create Interface VPC Endpoints in their VPCs.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS PrivateLink enables private unidirectional connectivity with zero CIDR overlap conflicts, and AWS WAF associates directly with Network Load Balancers to inspect incoming client traffic at Layer 7.

options.text: Deploy AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections between all 250 client VPCs and the vendor VPC, configuring static routes on all customer routers. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Managing 250 IPsec VPN connections creates immense administrative overhead and cannot handle overlapping private IP address ranges.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with an attached AWS WAF Web ACL as an AWS PrivateLink Endpoint Service allows clients to connect securely over Interface VPC Endpoints with full Layer 7 WAF protection and zero CIDR overlap.

options.text: Implantar um Network Load Balancer (NLB) na VPC do fornecedor, associar uma Web ACL do AWS WAF diretamente ao NLB e configurar o NLB como um serviço de endpoint do AWS PrivateLink. Orientar os clientes a criar Interface VPC Endpoints em suas VPCs.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A biomedical research lab runs distributed genomic analysis pipelines processing thousands of patient DNA sequence files stored in Amazon S3. Pipeline jobs require POSIX-compliant shared file storage capable of delivering hundreds of thousands of IOPS with sub-millisecond latencies, running containerized bioinformatics applications across hundreds of compute-optimized EC2 Spot instances, and automatically scaling compute resources down to zero when no jobs are pending. Which combination of actions meets these requirements with the LOWEST cost? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure AWS Batch compute environments using EC2 Spot Instances with an allocation strategy of SPOT_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED, and define containerized job definitions for the genomic analysis workloads.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Batch manages job queuing, dependencies, and dynamically provisions EC2 Spot instances with the SPOT_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED strategy to minimize interruptions and scale down to zero when idle.

options.text: Deploy 100 On-Demand EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group running 24/7, mounting an Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) standard volume via NFS.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running On-Demand instances 24/7 generates massive idle expenses, and NFS over standard EBS does not provide the sub-millisecond IOPS required for genomic processing.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system configured with a Data Repository Association (DRA) linked directly to the S3 genomics data lake bucket, mounting the file system inside the AWS Batch job container definitions.
options.explanation: Correct: FSx for Lustre Persistent/Scratch provides massive POSIX parallel throughput and hundreds of thousands of IOPS with sub-millisecond latencies, synchronizing seamlessly with Amazon S3.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon EMR cluster with 200 core nodes running Apache Hadoop and configure daily snapshot exports to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running a persistent 200-node EMR cluster incurs high baseline compute costs and does not support native containerized bioinformatics tools as easily as AWS Batch.

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 event notifications to invoke 50,000 unthrottled AWS Lambda functions simultaneously, storing intermediate binary matrices in local /tmp storage. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Lambda has a 10 GB ephemeral /tmp limit and 15-minute execution limit that will fail when executing large multi-hour genomic alignment workloads.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying AWS Batch compute environments configured with EC2 Spot Instances enables automated containerized job execution with scale-to-zero capabilities. Provisioning an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system with a Data Repository Association to Amazon S3 provides high-performance POSIX storage for parallel genomic jobs.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A fintech payment gateway processes financial transactions that must be processed in strict sequential order per merchant account. The ingestion layer receives up to 50,000 transactions per second. The architecture must decouple payment producers from downstream authorization microservices, guarantee exact once-in-order execution per merchant ID, automatically isolate corrupted transaction payloads to a Dead-Letter Queue without blocking subsequent valid merchant transactions, and store audit records in a high-throughput NoSQL database. Which serverless architecture satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Send payment transactions to an Amazon SNS Standard topic configured to fan out to 20 AWS Lambda functions simultaneously without error handling.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon SNS Standard topics do not guarantee message ordering and lack native DLQ partition isolation for sequential transaction processing.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance running RabbitMQ in a public subnet, writing transaction records to a local MySQL database with manual backup scripts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed RabbitMQ on EC2 creates single points of failure, scaling bottlenecks at 50k TPS, and requires extensive maintenance.

options.text: Stream payment records into Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose configured with a 15-minute buffer interval, delivering raw files to Amazon S3 Standard. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: A 15-minute buffer delay fails the real-time transaction processing requirement and does not support sub-second sequential payment authorization.

options.text: Publish payment transaction messages to an Amazon SQS FIFO queue with MessageGroupId set to the MerchantID and MessageDeduplicationId enabled. Configure an AWS Lambda function as an event source mapping with BisectBatchOnFunctionError enabled, configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) with maxReceiveCount set to 3, and write processed payment transactions to Amazon DynamoDB.
options.explanation: Correct: SQS FIFO preserves strict message ordering within each MessageGroupId, while Lambda with BisectBatchOnFunctionError isolates poisoned batches and routes failed items to a DLQ without halting downstream valid transactions.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon SQS FIFO queues with MessageGroupId set to MerchantID, consumed by AWS Lambda with event source mapping configured with BisectBatchOnFunctionError and Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) redrive policies, writing to Amazon DynamoDB fulfills ordered, resilient event processing.

options.text: Create Gateway VPC Endpoints for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB in all 50 VPCs and associate the endpoints with all private subnet route tables.

options.text: Replace all private subnets with public subnets and attach public Elastic IP addresses to all EC2 instances. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Placing backend microservices and databases in public subnets exposes resources to the public internet, violating security compliance policies.

options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudFront incurs data transfer out charges and public internet routing introduces security exposure and unnecessary latency for internal microservices.

questions.generalExplanation: Creating free Gateway VPC Endpoints for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB in all VPC route tables automatically routes traffic across the internal AWS network at zero cost per GB, eliminating NAT Gateway data processing fees.

questions.statement: A technology enterprise runs polyglot microservices across Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda. Which combination of actions should the lead architect implement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure microservices to write log lines to local container storage and run a scheduled cron job to upload files to Amazon S3 hourly.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Writing logs locally and uploading hourly introduces severe data lag and lacks real-time distributed trace propagation.

options.text: Deploy the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) collector as a sidecar container in ECS Fargate task definitions, instrumenting applications using OpenTelemetry SDKs with W3C Trace Context.
options.explanation: Correct: ADOT provides an open-standard, CNCF-compliant collector that captures distributed traces and metrics with standard W3C Context propagation across containerized microservices.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon DynamoDB table in each region to store custom span IDs and run Athena SQL queries every 5 minutes. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Building a custom tracing engine on DynamoDB and Athena requires immense custom development and maintenance compared to managed tracing tools.

options.text: Enable AWS CloudTrail data events for all S3 buckets and configure Amazon QuickSight dashboards to monitor HTTP latency. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudTrail tracks management and object API calls; it does not collect microservice application-layer HTTP traces or distributed span context.

options.text: Configure the ADOT collector to export distributed traces to AWS X-Ray and enable Amazon CloudWatch ServiceLens with Container Insights to correlate traces, logs, and container metrics.
options.explanation: Correct: CloudWatch ServiceLens seamlessly combines AWS X-Ray distributed trace graphs with CloudWatch Container Insights metrics and logs in a unified service dependency map.

questions.statement: An online ticketing system experiences massive, sudden traffic spikes during flash sales. The application runs on Amazon ECS on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. In past events, Auto Scaling groups based on CPU utilization scaled too slowly, causing HTTP 504 gateway timeout errors. The architecture must scale tasks in under 1 minute, minimize compute expenses during normal baseline traffic using EC2 Spot Instances, and automatically provision underlying EC2 instances in synchronization with pending ECS tasks. Which architecture fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Configure an ECS service on AWS Fargate with a scheduled scaling policy that increases task count to maximum limits 24 hours prior to sales.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Scheduled scaling requires knowing surge times in advance and running maximum Fargate capacity for 24 hours results in excessive unnecessary costs.

options.text: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group of On-Demand instances with simple scaling based on NetworkIn CloudWatch alarms with a 10-minute cooldown. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Simple scaling with 10-minute cooldowns reacts too slowly to sudden spikes, and NetworkIn does not reflect web request concurrency.

options.text: Configure ECS Capacity Providers with Managed Scaling and Managed Termination Protection, backed by an Auto Scaling group using a mixed instances policy with Spot and On-Demand instances. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling using target tracking based on the Application Load Balancer RequestCountPerTarget metric.
options.explanation: Correct: ECS Capacity Providers automatically scale the EC2 cluster according to pending container placement demands, while target tracking on ALB RequestCountPerTarget scales task count before CPU saturation.

options.text: Deploy static EC2 Metal instances in a spread placement group and configure cron jobs to launch containers via SSH. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Static bare-metal instances with manual SSH scripts is an expensive, unscalable, high-overhead operational anti-pattern.

questions.generalExplanation: Configuring ECS Capacity Providers with Managed Scaling and Managed Instance Protection on a mixed-instance Auto Scaling group, paired with ECS Service Auto Scaling target tracking on the ALB RequestCountPerTarget metric, enables responsive, cost-effective scaling.

options.text: Increase the max_connections parameter to 50,000 in the custom DB parameter group and write a custom Lambda function to monitor database activity.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Setting max_connections excessively high consumes massive memory on the DB instance and leads to out-of-memory crashes, while custom Lambda monitoring scripts introduce operational overhead.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster as a write-through cache and configure Aurora read replicas with manual vertical scale-up scripts. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Write-through Redis caches do not solve connection pooling for transactional write queries in PostgreSQL and manual scale-up scripts do not react fast enough during sudden spikes.

options.text: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables and configure Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canaries to monitor read request latency. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Migrating a complex relational PostgreSQL database to DynamoDB requires complete application rewrite, violating standard continuous improvement operational constraints.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying Amazon RDS Proxy between AWS Lambda functions and Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL manages connection pooling, while enabling Amazon DevOps Guru for RDS proactively detects performance anomalies and lock contention using machine learning.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: A multinational enterprise manages 200 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. Corporate cybersecurity compliance mandates that all application logs, operating system audit logs, and VPC Flow Logs generated in member accounts must be continuously streamed to a centralized Security Account in real time. In the Security Account, logs must be ingested into an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster for 30-day interactive analysis and simultaneously stored in an encrypted Amazon S3 data lake bucket with immutable storage for 7-year regulatory compliance. Which architecture meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Install Amazon OpenSearch Service Logstash agents on every EC2 instance in all 200 member accounts, configuring agents to output logs directly over public HTTPS endpoints.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Installing and maintaining third-party agents on thousands of instances across 200 accounts creates massive operational maintenance and exposes ingestion endpoints to the public internet.

options.text: Create AWS Lambda functions in every member account triggered by CloudWatch Logs to read log batches and call OpenSearch Index APIs synchronously.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Custom Lambda functions in 200 accounts incur high execution costs, introduce throttling risks under log surges, and require custom error handling.

options.text: Configure VPC Flow Logs to write to local S3 buckets in each member account, using AWS DataSync scheduled hourly tasks to replicate logs to the Security Account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: DataSync hourly sync introduces a 1-hour delay, failing the real-time streaming mandate, and requires managing 200 separate S3 buckets.

options.text: Create a centralized Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream in the Security Account configured with destinations to Amazon OpenSearch Service and the compliance S3 bucket. Create a CloudWatch Logs cross-account Destination in the Security Account, and deploy CloudWatch Logs Subscription Filters across all member accounts pointing to the central Destination.
options.explanation: Correct: CloudWatch Logs Subscription Filters natively stream log events cross-account into a Kinesis Data Firehose stream in the Security Account, which automatically buffers, formats, and delivers logs to OpenSearch for searching and S3 for compliance storage.

questions.generalExplanation: Configuring CloudWatch Logs Subscription Filters in member accounts using cross-account destination permissions pointing to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose stream in the Security Account delivers logs simultaneously to Amazon OpenSearch Service and Amazon S3 with zero per-account proxy infrastructure.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: A financial institution stores 5 PB of critical audit records in Amazon S3. SEC regulations dictate that the audit records must be strictly immutable (WORM - Write Once Read Many) for 10 years, ensuring that neither standard IAM administrators nor the AWS account root user can delete or overwrite objects during the retention duration. Access patterns show that records are accessed frequently for the first 30 days, rarely between 31 and 365 days, and accessed once every few years thereafter. Which storage architecture satisfies these regulatory requirements with the LOWEST cost?

options.text: Enable S3 Versioning, configure S3 Lifecycle to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days, and apply an S3 Bucket Policy with an explicit Deny on s3:DeleteObject for all IAM users.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Bucket policies can be modified or deleted by the account root user or administrators with s3:PutBucketPolicy permissions, failing SEC WORM compliance requirements.

options.text: Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance Mode with a 10-year retention period on an S3 Standard bucket. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Governance Mode allows users with s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permissions to delete objects, violating the strict non-bypassable compliance mandate.

options.text: Enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode with a default 10-year retention period on the S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days and to S3 Glacier Flexible Archive after 365 days.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode guarantees that objects cannot be overwritten or deleted by any user (including the AWS root account) until the retention period expires, while S3 Lifecycle automates tiered cost reduction.

options.text: Deploy an AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK) with automatic annual key rotation and store files in S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 One Zone-IA lacks multi-AZ resilience and KMS key rotation does not prevent object deletion by authorized administrators.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode enforces strict, non-bypassable WORM retention that prevents deletion by all users including root. S3 Lifecycle transitions objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering and Glacier Flexible Archive to optimize storage costs.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: An enterprise plans to migrate 600 VMware virtual machines from an on-premises data center to Amazon EC2 over an existing 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The migration must execute with continuous block-level data replication, enable non-disruptive launch testing of target EC2 instances prior to final cutover, automate post-launch driver and SSM agent installation, and require a cutover maintenance window of less than 15 minutes per server batch. Which migration strategy satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Export virtual machines as VMDK files, upload them to Amazon S3 using AWS DataSync, and call the VM Import/Export CLI operation. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exporting VMDKs and uploading via DataSync takes days, requires taking offline snapshots with significant downtime, and exceeds the 15-minute cutover window.

options.text: Install the AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) Replication Agent on all on-premises source virtual machines to perform continuous, block-level data replication over Direct Connect. Perform non-disruptive launch test instances in AWS to validate applications, and execute final cutover during the scheduled maintenance window.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) provides continuous asynchronous block-level replication, enables non-disruptive pre-cutover testing, and executes final server cutover in minutes with negligible downtime.

options.text: Deploy the AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) connector in vCenter to take snapshot backups of source VMs into Amazon S3. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS SMS is legacy and snapshot-based, whereas AWS MGN provides real-time continuous block-level replication and automated post-launch script execution.

options.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate virtual machine operating system disks to Amazon EBS gp3 volumes. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS DMS is designed for database migrations; it cannot replicate operating systems, system state, or bootable virtual machines.

questions.generalExplanation: Installing the AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) Replication Agent on source servers enables continuous, block-level data replication, non-disruptive testing, and fast final cutover with automated post-launch configuration.

Executar testes de inicialização não disruptivos na AWS para validar as aplicações e executar o corte final (cutover) durante a janela de manutenção agendada.
