questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A commercial enterprise is migrating an on-premises 12 TB Oracle database containing complex relational schemas, PL/SQL packages, and triggers to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The business requires continuous operational uptime on the source database during migration, automated conversion of database schemas and stored procedures, continuous ongoing transaction replication until the final maintenance cutover, and a cutover downtime window under 10 minutes. Which combination of tools and steps should the lead database architect implement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to analyze database objects, generate a migration assessment report, and automatically convert Oracle schema, stored procedures, functions, and triggers to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL dialect.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS SCT is specifically built for heterogeneous database migrations, automating the conversion of Oracle relational schemas, data types, and PL/SQL code to PostgreSQL-compatible PL/pgSQL.

options.text: Export all Oracle tables using Oracle Data Pump (expdp) to CSV files, transfer them using AWS Snowball Edge, and import data into Aurora PostgreSQL using pg_restore.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Oracle Data Pump to Snowball requires offline exports or introduces static data lag that cannot capture real-time transactions occurring during shipping.

options.text: Deploy AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) to perform block-level replication of the Oracle database server storage directly into the Aurora PostgreSQL shared storage volume.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS MGN is a block-level server migration tool; it cannot perform heterogeneous schema conversion from Oracle database engine to PostgreSQL engine.

options.text: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance and configure a migration task with Full Load plus Change Data Capture (CDC) with validation enabled to continuously replicate ongoing changes until cutover.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS DMS with CDC continuously captures live Oracle transactional redo changes and applies them in real time to Aurora PostgreSQL, allowing business operations to continue on-premises until the final low-downtime cutover.

options.text: Configure Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL as an Oracle Data Guard physical standby database, establishing synchronous redo transport over AWS Direct Connect. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Oracle Data Guard is a proprietary Oracle disaster recovery feature that operates strictly between identical Oracle database instances; it cannot replicate to PostgreSQL engines.

questions.generalExplanation: Using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert Oracle PL/SQL schemas and stored procedures to Aurora PostgreSQL dialect, combined with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) executing Full Load plus ongoing Change Data Capture (CDC), enables near-zero downtime heterogeneous database migration.

The business requires continuous operational uptime on the source database during migration, automated conversion of database schemas and stored procedures, continuous ongoing transaction replication until the final maintenance cutover, and a cutover downtime window under 10 minutes. Which combination of tools and steps should the lead database architect implement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to analyze database objects, generate a migration assessment report, and automatically convert Oracle schema, stored procedures, functions, and triggers to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL dialect.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS SCT is specifically built for heterogeneous database migrations, automating the conversion of Oracle relational schemas, data types, and PL/SQL code to PostgreSQL-compatible PL/pgSQL.

options.text: Export all Oracle tables using Oracle Data Pump (expdp) to CSV files, transfer them using AWS Snowball Edge, and import data into Aurora PostgreSQL using pg_restore.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Oracle Data Pump to Snowball requires offline exports or introduces static data lag that cannot capture real-time transactions occurring during shipping.

options.text: Deploy AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) to perform block-level replication of the Oracle database server storage directly into the Aurora PostgreSQL shared storage volume.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS MGN is a block-level server migration tool; it cannot perform heterogeneous schema conversion from Oracle database engine to PostgreSQL engine.

options.text: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance and configure a migration task with Full Load plus Change Data Capture (CDC) with validation enabled to continuously replicate ongoing changes until cutover.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS DMS with CDC continuously captures live Oracle transactional redo changes and applies them in real time to Aurora PostgreSQL, allowing business operations to continue on-premises until the final low-downtime cutover.

options.text: Configure Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL as an Oracle Data Guard physical standby database, establishing synchronous redo transport over AWS Direct Connect. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Oracle Data Guard is a proprietary Oracle disaster recovery feature that operates strictly between identical Oracle database instances; it cannot replicate to PostgreSQL engines.

en.generalExplanation: Using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert Oracle PL/SQL schemas and stored procedures to Aurora PostgreSQL dialect, combined with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) executing Full Load plus ongoing Change Data Capture (CDC), enables near-zero downtime heterogeneous database migration.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: An enterprise is decomposing an on-premises legacy monolithic banking system into containerized microservices running on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate across multiple AWS accounts using the Strangler Fig pattern. Client applications must continue calling a single unified endpoint. Traffic for newly modernized endpoints (such as /orders and /inventory) must be routed to the new microservices in AWS, while un-migrated legacy traffic continues routing to the on-premises application without code modifications to the legacy monolith. Which architecture should the solutions architect deploy?

options.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 Weighted Routing to route 50% of DNS queries to on-premises servers and 50% to AWS Application Load Balancers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Route 53 Weighted Routing distributes DNS resolution across all traffic randomly; it cannot inspect URL request paths (/orders vs /inventory) to route specific microservice endpoints.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda@Edge function on Amazon CloudFront to rewrite incoming HTTP requests and forward packets over public internet VPN connections. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Lambda@Edge cannot route requests directly to private RFC 1918 subnets or on-premises networks over private Direct Connect connections without complex public proxies.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces environment spanning the legacy network account and new microservices accounts. Create a Refactor Spaces application with an Amazon API Gateway proxy and define path-based routing rules that route specific endpoint paths to ECS Fargate services while sending default traffic to the on-premises legacy endpoint.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces is purpose-built to accelerate the Strangler Fig pattern across multiple AWS accounts, automatically provisioning and orchestrating API Gateway, Transit Gateway, and private Network Load Balancers to route traffic incrementally.

options.text: Rewrite all monolithic business logic into Amazon DynamoDB transactional stored procedures and eliminate the legacy database entirely. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store that does not support relational stored procedures or SQL dialect, requiring destructive refactoring.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces provisions an isolated multi-account routing boundary with managed API Gateway and Transit Gateway infrastructure, enabling path-based traffic routing between legacy applications and new microservices.

options.text: Implantar uma função AWS Lambda@Edge no Amazon CloudFront para reescrever requisições HTTP de entrada e encaminhar pacotes sobre conexões VPN pela internet pública.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O Lambda@Edge não consegue rotear requisições diretamente para sub-redes privadas RFC 1918 ou redes on-premises sobre Direct Connect privado sem proxies públicos complexos.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: An enterprise is migrating 4 PB of unstructured engineering design files from on-premises NetApp SAN/NAS storage to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP over an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. The file system contains hundreds of millions of files with complex POSIX and SMB NTFS permissions, hard links, symlinks, extended attributes, and ownership metadata. The migration must execute automated incremental synchronizations during business hours with bandwidth limits to prevent saturating production traffic, guarantee file metadata fidelity upon cutover, and minimize custom synchronization scripts. Which migration architecture should the solutions architect deploy?

options.text: Order 45 AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices, manually copy files using the Snowball Client, physically ship the devices to AWS, and import data directly into an Amazon S3 Standard bucket.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Snowball Edge devices take weeks to ship, do not support incremental live synchronization before cutover, and importing into S3 does not preserve native NetApp ONTAP filesystem structures directly.

options.text: Deploy an EC2 instance running rsync over an IPsec VPN tunnel connected to the on-premises NAS, executing a shell script that transfers files to Amazon Elastic File System (EFS).
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard single-threaded rsync over VPN is extremely slow for hundreds of millions of files across 4 PB, fails to preserve Windows SMB NTFS permissions accurately, and targets EFS instead of the required FSx for ONTAP.

options.text: Use the S3 File Gateway of AWS Storage Gateway deployed as a virtual appliance in vSphere, copying data to an S3 bucket and triggering Lambda functions to convert files into FSx volumes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 File Gateway is designed for hybrid file-to-object tiering; it does not perform automated multi-threaded parallel replication to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with metadata fidelity.

options.text: Deploy AWS DataSync agents in the on-premises VMware environment. Create an AWS DataSync task targeting the on-premises NFS/SMB shares as the source location and the Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system as the destination location, configuring bandwidth throttling schedules and full metadata preservation verification.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS DataSync uses a purpose-built network protocol to parallelize data transfers up to 10 Gbps, natively preserves all POSIX/SMB permissions, timestamps, and extended attributes, and provides automated task scheduling with bandwidth throttling during business hours.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying AWS DataSync agents on-premises connected to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides high-performance parallelized data transfer, preserves complete POSIX/SMB metadata and permissions, supports automated scheduling with bandwidth throttling, and performs end-to-end data integrity validation.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A global financial corporation operates an IBM z/OS mainframe executing critical nightly batch processing jobs written in COBOL against VSAM files and DB2 databases. The enterprise is modernizing this workload to the AWS Cloud to eliminate multimillion-dollar mainframe licensing costs while enabling modern SQL-based analytics on historical transactions. The target architecture must support running re-platformed COBOL batch applications with high reliability, automated job scheduling, and transformed analytics storage utilizing an open-table format (Apache Iceberg) on Amazon S3 with sub-minute query response times in Amazon Athena. Which modernized architecture should the enterprise deploy?

options.text: Deploy the COBOL batch applications using AWS Mainframe Modernization service with the Micro Focus (replatform) managed runtime environment. Ingest batch output files using AWS Glue ETL jobs that transform data into Apache Iceberg table format registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog on Amazon S3, and query transactional datasets using Amazon Athena.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Mainframe Modernization service provides a managed runtime to replatform COBOL applications with automated batch job scheduling and high availability. AWS Glue transforms and catalogs data into open Apache Iceberg format on S3 for low-cost, high-performance Athena SQL queries.

options.text: Emulate the mainframe architecture by launching an Amazon EC2 Mac instance, installing a custom open-source COBOL compiler, and writing output records to local EBS volumes queried via SQLite.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running custom emulators on EC2 Mac instances lacks enterprise support, job scheduling reliability, horizontal scalability, and integration with modern distributed cloud data lakes.

options.text: Rewrite all COBOL batch business logic into AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda functions within 30 days, storing all transaction history in Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Streams enabled.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Completely rewriting millions of lines of complex COBOL business logic in 30 days is exceptionally high-risk and impractical, and DynamoDB is not optimized for ad-hoc analytical SQL scans.

options.text: Maintain the on-premises IBM mainframe permanently, install AWS Direct Connect, and configure on-premises DB2 databases to push change logs over IPsec VPN tunnels to Amazon RDS for MySQL.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Maintaining the on-premises mainframe permanently fails the objective to eliminate multimillion-dollar mainframe licensing costs, and replication over VPN does not provide a modern open-table analytics lake.

questions.generalExplanation: Using AWS Mainframe Modernization (Replatform with Micro Focus runtime) to execute legacy COBOL batch applications on AWS, transforming output files with AWS Glue ETL into Apache Iceberg format on Amazon S3, and querying via Amazon Athena provides a fully modernized, cost-effective architecture.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A multinational enterprise connects its primary corporate data center to 100 AWS VPCs across multiple AWS Regions using a single 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. Due to rapid business growth, data transfer bandwidth is nearing 100% capacity. The network engineering team must upgrade connectivity to a resilient 10 Gbps infrastructure with active-active link aggregation, automated link failover without BGP reconvergence delays, and support for adding up to 4 parallel dedicated 10 Gbps connections in a single Link Aggregation Group (LAG). Which hybrid architecture should the network architect deploy?

options.text: Deploy 10 individual 1 Gbps IPsec VPN tunnels across the public internet and configure ECMP routing on a local customer gateway router.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Internet VPN tunnels have bandwidth caps (1.25 Gbps per tunnel), suffer unpredictable internet latency, and cannot aggregate dedicated physical Direct Connect ports into a LAG.

options.text: Provision a new Link Aggregation Group (LAG) consisting of dedicated 10 Gbps Direct Connect connections across two distinct Direct Connect locations. Associate the LAG connections with a centralized Direct Connect Gateway using Transit Virtual Interfaces (Transit VIFs) attached to regional AWS Transit Gateways.
options.explanation: Correct: Direct Connect LAG bundles up to four 10 Gbps or 100 Gbps dedicated physical connections into a single logical interface at Layer 2, delivering up to 40 Gbps of aggregated active-active bandwidth with seamless failover and multi-region Transit Gateway routing.

options.text: Provision 100 Private Virtual Interfaces (Private VIFs) on the existing 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection and enable BGP multi-hop routing. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Direct Connect connections support a maximum of 50 Private VIFs and adding virtual interfaces does not increase the underlying 1 Gbps physical port capacity.

options.text: Create an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in each VPC, connecting on-premises SAN arrays over public HTTPS endpoints. This architectural configuration step ensures full compliance with AWS Well-Architected Framework enterprise best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway Volume Gateway is for iSCSI block storage tiering; it does not provide general network layer routing or physical port bandwidth aggregation for VPC workloads.

questions.generalExplanation: Provisioning a 10 Gbps Link Aggregation Group (LAG) on dedicated Direct Connect ports at two distinct Direct Connect locations and associating them with a Direct Connect Gateway provides scalable, highly resilient active-active bandwidth scaling.

pt.statement: Uma empresa multinacional conecta seu data center corporativo principal a 100 VPCs na AWS em múltiplas Regiões AWS usando uma única conexão dedicada de 1 Gbps do AWS Direct Connect. Devido ao rápido crescimento dos negócios, a largura de banda de transferência de dados está próxima de 100% da capacidade. A equipe de engenharia de rede deve atualizar a conectividade para uma infraestrutura resiliente de 10 Gbps com agregação de links ativo-ativo, failover automático de link sem atrasos de reconvergência BGP e suporte para adicionar até 4 conexões dedicadas paralelas de 10 Gbps em um único Link Aggregation Group (LAG). Qual arquitetura híbrida o arquiteto de rede deve implantar?

options.text: Implantar 10 túneis VPN IPsec individuais de 1 Gbps pela internet pública e configurar roteamento ECMP em um roteador de customer gateway local.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Túneis VPN pela internet possuem limites de largura de banda (1,25 Gbps por túnel), sofrem com latência imprevisível da internet e não conseguem agregar portas físicas dedicadas do Direct Connect em um LAG.

options.text: Provisionar um novo Link Aggregation Group (LAG) composto por conexões dedicadas de 10 Gbps do Direct Connect em dois locais distintos do Direct Connect. Associar as conexões LAG a um Direct Connect Gateway centralizado usando Transit Virtual Interfaces (Transit VIFs) anexadas a AWS Transit Gateways regionais.
options.explanation: Correto: O Direct Connect LAG agrupa até quatro conexões físicas dedicadas de 10 Gbps ou 100 Gbps em uma única interface lógica na Camada 2, fornecendo até 40 Gbps de largura de banda agregada ativo-ativo com failover transparente e roteamento multirregião via Transit Gateway.

options.text: Provisionar 100 Private Virtual Interfaces (Private VIFs) na conexão existente de 1 Gbps do Direct Connect e habilitar roteamento BGP multi-hop. Esta etapa de configuração arquitetural garante total conformidade com as melhores práticas corporativas do AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Conexões do Direct Connect suportam um máximo de 50 Private VIFs e adicionar interfaces virtuais não aumenta a capacidade física da porta de 1 Gbps.

options.text: Criar um AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway em cada VPC, conectando storages SAN on-premises sobre endpoints HTTPS públicos. Esta etapa de configuração arquitetural garante total conformidade com as melhores práticas corporativas do AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O Storage Gateway Volume Gateway foi projetado para armazenamento de blocos iSCSI em nuvem; ele não fornece roteamento de camada de rede nem agregação de largura de banda física para cargas de trabalho de VPC.

pt.generalExplanation: O provisionamento de um Link Aggregation Group (LAG) de 10 Gbps em portas dedicadas do Direct Connect em dois locais distintos do Direct Connect associados a um Direct Connect Gateway fornece escalabilidade e resiliência com agregação de banda ativo-ativo.
